## What you must confirm, each against the source

1. **`FIRST_IMPORTED_CTE` has no `created_at` filter of any kind.** This is the decision the whole ticket turns on. Every other column on /scenes is clamped to the `?days=` window; this one is all-time on purpose, because a `min()` over the windowed CTE can never return a date older than the window — on the default 30-day view every scene would report a first import inside the last month, the column would rank nothing, and it would look entirely plausible in a screenshot. Read the constant and confirm the predicate is absent. Also confirm `ACQUIRED_CTE` still carries its window on **both** of its union halves — the fix must not have leaked the other way.

2. **The key expression is character-for-character the one the other CTEs group by.** `lower(btrim(scene_title))`. A key differing by so much as a `btrim` left-joins to nothing, and the column would be an em dash on every row that has a date. Check the guard too (`scene_title is not null and btrim(scene_title) <> ''`), on both halves.

3. **The header order matches Eric's table**, in the source, as a sequence: Scene, Imported, First imported, Last imported, Users recorded, Sessions, Last recorded. Then check the **body cells are written in that same order** — seven right headings over seven wrong columns is silent and total. Check `colSpan` is 7.

4. **The default sort is `last_recorded` in both files and they agree**: `listScenes` in `admin/src/lib/scenes.ts` and the page's own fallback in `admin/src/app/scenes/page.tsx`. If they disagree the arrow points at one column while the rows are ordered by another, and each half looks right alone.

5. **My new test would actually fail against a windowed `min`.** I built the broken version and confirmed it — `the first import is a min over a CTE with no window at all` failed with "First imported must not be clamped to the window", while the `min(created_at)` assertion on the line above **passed** against the bug. Verify the assertions are genuinely capable of that rather than taking my word: read the test and satisfy yourself. If you want to reproduce it, add the predicate back temporarily and revert it — you have no deliverables, so if you do, you MUST leave the tree exactly as you found it; `git diff` must be unchanged when you finish. Simply reading the assertions is an acceptable substitute and is the safer choice.

6. **The one-round-trip rule holds.** `admin/CLAUDE.md` records a production 504 on 2026-08-20 and a pool of three in `admin/src/lib/db.ts`; `test/server/admin-pool.test.mjs` fails the build on any concurrent promise under `admin/src`.
